Rashi on Berakhot 32b:10:1.hebrew: קוה - והתחזק, ולא תמשוך ידך, אלא חזור וקוה:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:10:1.english: Hope - And strengthen yourself, and do not withdraw your hand; rather, return and hope.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:11:1.hebrew: צריכין חזוק - שיתחזק אדם בהן תמיד בכל כחו:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:11:1.english: Require strengthening - That a person should constantly strengthen himself in them with all his might.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:11:2.hebrew: דרך ארץ - אם אומן הוא לאומנתו, אם סוחר הוא לסחורתו, אם איש מלחמה הוא למלחמתו:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:11:2.english: Occupation - If he is a craftsman, [he must bolster himself] in his craft; if he is a merchant, in his trade; if he is a warrior, in his warfare.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:16:1.hebrew: שלשים חיל - ראשי גייסות וחבורות חלוקות:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:16:1.english: Thirty armies - Divisions of troops and distinct companies.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:16:2.hebrew: לגיון וקרטון וגסטרא - שמות של שררה, כגון שלטון והגמון ודוכס ופחה:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:16:2.english: Ligyon and karton and gastera - [These are] titles of authority, such as ruler, hegemon, duke, and governor.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:17:1.english: Her burnt-offering - Like burnt-offerings and sacrifices.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:17:2.hebrew: גם אלה - מעשה העגל, שאמרו: ״אלה אלהיך ישראל״ (שמות ל״ב:ד׳):
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:17:2.english: These too - [This refers to] the incident of the [Golden] Calf, regarding which they said: “These are your gods, Israel” (Exodus 32:4).

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:19:1.hebrew: ואנכי זה מעשה סיני - שנאמר בו: "אנכי ה' אלהיך" (שמות כ׳:ב׳):
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:19:1.english: “And I” — that is the event of Sinai - As it is said regarding it: “I am the Lord your God” (Exodus 20:2).

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:1:1.hebrew: עלה ראש הפסגה - בדבר תפלה זו, נתרציתי להראותך אותה:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:1:1.english: Go up to the top of the summit - In the matter of this prayer, I have consented to show it [the Land] to you.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:21:1.english: Those who dwell in Your House - And afterwards, "they will praise You."

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:22:1.hebrew: יודו לשמך - והדר, ישבו ישרים את פניך:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:22:1.english: Will give thanks unto Your name - And afterwards, “the upright will sit before You.”

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:24:1.english: Nine hours - [Three hours each] for the three prayers.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:25:1.hebrew: תורתם משתמרת - בתוך לבם, שאין תלמודם משתכח:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:25:1.english: Their Torah is preserved - Within their hearts, for their learning is not forgotten.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:27:1.hebrew: אבל למלכי עכו"ם פוסק - שלא יהרגנו:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:27:1.english: However, for gentile kings, he interrupts - So that [the king] will not kill him.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:29:1.hebrew: הא דאפשר בקצור - כגון שסמוך לגמור תפלתו:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:29:1.english: This [case] where it is possible to abridge - For example, when he is close to finishing his prayer.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:3:1.hebrew: ובפרשכם כפיכם - אי לאו דגדולה תפלה, כיון דאמר "למה לי רוב זבחיכם", למה לי תו "ובפרשכם"? הא אפילו זבחיהם לא ניחא ליה:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:3:1.english: And when you spread forth your hands - Were it not that prayer is greater [than sacrifices] — once He said, “To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?”, why do I further need “And when you spread forth [your hands]”? For even their sacrifices are not pleasing to Him!

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:5:1.hebrew: אל תחרש - מדלא כתיב "את דמעתי תראה", ש"מ נראית היא לפניו, ואין צריך להתפלל אלא שתתקבל לפניו:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:5:1.english: Keep not silence - Since it is not written, “See my tears,” learn from this that they are visible before Him, and there is no need to pray except that they be accepted before Him.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:7:1.hebrew: ונתתה אותה קיר ברזל - סימן למחיצת ברזל המפסקת בינו לבינם:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:7:1.english: And set it as an iron wall - [This was] a sign of an iron partition separating between Him and them.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:9:1.hebrew: ומעיין בה - מצפה שתעשה בקשתו על ידי הארכתו. סוף שאינה נעשית, ונמצאת תוחלת ממושכה חנם, והיא כאב לב — כשאדם מצפה ואין תאותו באה:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:9:1.english: And expects [it to be answered] - He anticipates that his request will be fulfilled through his prolonging [it]. Ultimately, it is not fulfilled, and it turns out to be hope deferred in vain, which is heartache — when a person anticipates, but his desire does not come.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:9:2.english: Hope - An expression of entreaty and supplication.

Rashi on Berakhot 32b:9:3.hebrew: ועץ חיים תאוה באה - סופו של מקרא הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 32b:9:3.english: And a tree of life is desire fulfilled - This is the end of the [same] verse.

Tosafot on Berakhot 32b:1:1.hebrew: גדולה תפלה יותר ממעשים טובים - בלא תפלה, שהרי משה רבינו ע"ה, אף על פי שהיו בידו מעשים טובים, הוצרך לתפלה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 32b:1:1.english: Prayer is greater than good deeds - [Meaning, than good deeds] without prayer; for Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, even though he had good deeds to his credit, needed prayer.

Tosafot on Berakhot 32b:23:1.hebrew: קודם תפלתו מנין שנא' אשרי יושבי ביתך - ולפיכך תקנו לומר זה הפסוק קודם ״תהלה לדוד״, לאפוקי מהנהו דאמרי ״אשרי״ הרבה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 32b:23:1.english: "Before his prayer, from where [is it derived]? As it is stated: 'Happy are those who dwell in Your House'" - And therefore, they instituted reciting this verse before Tehillah LeDavid [Psalm 145], to exclude [the practice of] those who recite many [verses of] Ashrei.

Tosafot on Berakhot 32b:5:1.hebrew: אל דמעתי אל תחרש - פרש"י דדייק מדיוקא: מדלא קאמר "ודמעתי תראה", ש"מ שהיא נראית בכל פעם, ואין להתפלל רק שתתקבל:
Tosafot on Berakhot 32b:5:1.english: At my tears keep not silence - Rashi explained that [the Gemara] deduces from the precision [of the verse]: since it does not say, “and see my tears,” learn from this that it is seen every time, and one need only pray that it be accepted.

Tosafot on Berakhot 32b:9:1.hebrew: כל המאריך בתפלתו ומעיין בה - פירוש: שמצפה שתבא בקשתו, לפי שכוון בתפלתו. תימה, דהכא משמע דעיון תפלה לאו מעליותא הוא! וכן משמע פ' הרואה (לקמן ברכות נה.): "ג' דברים מזכירין עונותיו של אדם", וקאמר עיון תפלה. ולא כן משמע בפ' מפנין (שבת קכז.), דקאמר: "אדם אוכל פירותיהן בעוה"ז", וקא חשיב עיון תפלה — אלמא מעליותא הוא! וכן משמע בגט פשוט (ב"ב קסד:), דקאמר: "משלשה דברים אין אדם ניצול בכל יום", וקאמר עיון תפלה — פירוש: שאין אדם מעיין בה; אם כן, משמע שהוא טוב. וי"ל, דתרי עיון תפלה יש: עיון תפלה דהכא — המצפה שתבא בקשתו, ועיון תפלה דהתם — שמכוין את לבו לתפלה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 32b:9:1.english: "Anyone who prolongs his prayer and expects it to be answered" - Explanation: That he anticipates that his petition will be fulfilled because he concentrated in his prayer. This is astonishing, for here it implies that iyyun tefillah is not a virtue! And so it implies in the chapter [entitled] HaRoeh (below, Berakhot 55a): "Three things cause a person’s sins to be recalled," and it mentions iyyun tefillah. Yet it does not imply so in the chapter [entitled] Mefanin (Shabbat 127a), where it states: "A person eats their fruits in this world..." and it includes iyyun tefillah — evidently it is a virtue! And so it implies in [the chapter entitled] Get Pashut (Bava Batra 164b), where it states: "From three things a person is not saved every day," and it mentions iyyun tefillah — explanation: that a person does not concentrate in it; if so, this implies that it is good! And it can be answered that there are two [types of] iyyun tefillah: the iyyun tefillah of here [refers to] one who anticipates that his petition will be fulfilled, while the iyyun tefillah of there [refers to] one who directs his heart to prayer.
